answer: Give every identity its own sealed replica: sealing runs a slow encode keyed by a salt drawn from that account's public key, so two agents on identical data still hold two different bytes. Each epoch draws a random delta of offsets and grading accepts only the offset proof served from the sealed file. Deduplication stops paying, since storage is charged per head and the seal is a cedar-expensive job no clone can pool. If a clone serves a range from a shared copy - a missed ledge - the seat voids, and the first delta catches whoever skipped sealing.
